cpmplus.w4molang.menu.formulas.desc: Replaces Molang formulas with plain linear keyframes on the animation's snapping grid (Ctrl+Z undoes)
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.warn: %s animation(s) use formulas. In game they become frame-by-frame movement (the same as the preview).
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.ifIgnored: Nothing to do: the export already writes the formula's values frame by frame.
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.tooltip: Formulas are sampled at the animation's snapping (Encaixe). More snapping = closer to the preview and a bigger file.
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.red: The formula in %s uses %s, which CPM does not have in game (animation %s). The game only gets a fixed recording of what the preview shows, not the real effect.
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.redIfIgnored: In game it never changes for real (no randomness, no variables). Use numbers or formulas with query.anim_time only.
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.none: No formulas found: every keyframe already holds plain numbers.
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.count: %s keyframe(s) with a formula -> about %s plain keyframes
cpmplus.w4molang.formula.hint: Only the stretches with a formula change; plain number keys stay as they are. Channels marked red use things the game can't reproduce and start unchecked. More snapping = more keyframes. Ctrl+Z undoes.
